title: Designing a notification system

facts.text: A messaging solution such as Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) can support the notification push; it is a cross-platform solution that composes, sends, queues and routes notifications reliably.
FCM provides a unified API between the message senders (app servers) and the receivers (client apps).
When the client app starts for the first time, it sends credentials to FCM, including the Sender ID, API Key and App ID.
FCM generates a registration token for the client app instance, so the token is also called the Instance ID; the token must be included in the notifications.
The client app sends the registration token to the app server, which caches it for subsequent communications.
Over time the app server has too many tokens to maintain, so the recommended practice is to store each token with a timestamp and remove stale tokens from time to time.
Messages can be composed directly in the console GUI or sent from the app server, using the Firebase Admin SDK or HTTP.
FCM receives the messages and queues them in storage if the devices are not online.
FCM forwards the messages to platform-level transport, which handles platform-specific configurations.
The messages are routed to the targeted devices, and the notifications can be displayed according to the configurations sent from the app server.

notes: thin: the guide covers only the push path through FCM; no requirements, other channels (SMS, email), scale or estimates, data model, API, retries or deduplication, rate limiting, or user preferences.
